Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.
source: North Bay Bohemian, Visit Santa Rosa

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

Dear Bay Area Writers and Authors:

Want to become a better writer, or finally turn that idea you've been sitting on for years into your first book? Trying to get noticed in a sea of indie and self-published authors? title: Park Rx—Intermediate Hiking for Fitness Fall 2026
location: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
description:
The program leaders will guide you on 8 weekly hikes with the challenge increasing each week. Leaders will have group discussions about gear, hydration, hiking poles, first aid and pacing, etc. The group's final hike aims for Bald Mountain, where hikers can enjoy stunning vistas.

The following is a list of possible routes specifically selected for this hiking series: 

1) Sat 9/26 — Creekside + Waterfall loop, 3.6 miles, 750 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 2) Sat 10/03 – Vista Trail loop, 3.4 miles, 830 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 3) Sat 10/10 – Hillside to Neptune table + Meadow, 4.4 miles, 970 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 4) Sat 10/17 – Goodspeed to Nattkemper bench, 3.8 miles, 1,240 ft elevation \[meet @ Goodspeed lot\] 5) Sat 10/24 – Hillside + Vista Trail loop, 3.6 miles, 1,070 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 6) Sat 10/31 – False Lake Meadow & Lake Ilsanjo loop in Trionne-Annadel SP, 6.1 miles, 670 ft elevation \[meet @ Annadel's Cobblestone Trailhead\] 7) Sat 11/07 – Fern Lake + Orchard loop in SDC/Jack London SHP, 5.5 miles, 1,460 ft elevation \[meet @ Walnut & North St inside SDC; park on Grove St\] 8) Sat 11/14 – Bald Mtn summit (w/optional Headwaters detour, 5.8 miles), 5.1 miles, 1,670 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\]

Please note these routes are subject to change based on the group and weather, as the group does hike in light rains. Wear appropriate footwear for rocky or slippery trails, and layers. Bring water, and if desired, a snack. The group will be limited to 35 participants. 

The hiking series costs $80 (plus a $10 parking fee per visit. Note that the Sugarloaf Annual Pass is $59 and valid at Sugarloaf and Jack London SHP), or free-of-cost for participants with a September 2026 or newer Park Rx from a Sonoma County Medical Provider.

title: "Paddle The Petaluma: Turn to The River" Guided Kayak Tour
location: The Floathouse Petaluma
description:
Paddle the Petaluma: Turn to The River is a relaxed, beginner-friendly guided kayak tour exploring the past, present, and future of Petaluma’s historic waterway. Launching right from downtown at The Floathouse Petaluma, you'll take part in this Sonoma County Signature Experience by spending about 90 minutes on the water in stable sit-on-top kayaks, traveling a gentle mile-and-a-half route through “Petaluma’s Longest Park.”

Along the way, you’ll raft up at docks around town, fascinating  landmarks, and riverfront gathering spaces to hear stories about how this Gold Rush-era “saltwater highway” helped shape Petaluma—and how today’s community is continuing to reinvent and reconnect with the river. This isn’t just a history tour. You’ll also learn about the people, businesses, artists, nonprofits, and river advocates helping shape the waterway’s future right now.

Everything is included in the $75 experience: kayak, gear, knowledgeable local guides, insider river stories, and post-paddle perks at nearby businesses. Finish with plenty of time for brunch, coffee, shopping, or simply hanging out downtown by the water. No experience necessary.

Note: The Floathouse Petaluma is a nonprofit project dedicated to “putting butts in boats and smiles on faces” by offering year-round easy access to the Petaluma River in and on people-powered water craft through rentals, events, classes, lessons and summer camps.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Home Ground Habitats Fall Celebration: Native Plant Sale and Tabling Event!
location: Home Ground Habitats
description:
On Saturday, October 17, from 10:00am-3:00pm, Home Ground Habitats will have our annual Fall Celebration to kick off the planting season.

Come celebrate with us at our open garden, tabling event, and fall plant sale! Fall is the best time of year to purchase native plants because the start of California’s rainy season is the ideal time to add new plants to the garden. Planting with the first rains gives roots the cool, wet winter months to settle in and become established before the warmer, drier seasons arrive. Shop 20% off all habitat plants, wildflower seeds, and more - give your garden a strong start for the year ahead.

Home Ground Habitats is a native plant nursery, demonstration garden, and education center located in Indian Valley, Novato, CA. As a community-centered organization, we focus on environmental education, California native plant propagation, and ethical land stewardship on nearly one acre of land. The demonstration gardens at Home Ground showcase a sustainable, organic approach to creating a truly California-friendly landscape using native plants and drought-tolerant Mediterranean species to increase biodiversity. We have native plant experts who can help anyone find the right plants to create a wildlife habitat garden in their own backyard. Our mission is to bring the natural world, pollinators, and wildlife to a landscape that also provides sustenance for humans.

As we celebrate the shifting of the season, our tabling event will offer information and educational resources about bringing biodiversity into your garden, supporting wildlife, creating beautiful pollinator habitats, and protecting the land around us. Expect to see our amazing community partners: Marin County Parks, Marin Monarch Working Group, Happy Bat Solutions, Pesticide Free Zone, Pollinator Partnership, California Bluebird Recovery Program, Museum of American Indian, and WildCare. Presentations will be scheduled throughout the day for even more learning.

Get your garden ready and plant it out with habitat plants that support pollinators and wildlife from Home Ground Habitats! RSVP to let us know you're coming. https://homegroundhabitats.org/event/fall-celebration-plant-sale-at-home-ground-habitats/

title: Intermediate Stained Glass - Photo Booth Frame
location: Art Escape
description:
Ready to take your stained glass skills to the next level? In this class, you'll expand your techniques by creating a beautiful stained glass photo booth frame that will hold a 2x6 photo and learn how to incorporate framing materials into your project.

You'll design your own unique pattern by selecting from a variety of pre-cut glass squares, copper foil, solder, clean, and finish your piece before attaching it to a frame.

This class is ideal for students who have completed a beginner stained glass class or have basic experience with copper foil and soldering.

All materials and tools are provided. Glass colors and textures will vary, making every frame a one-of-a-kind creation. 

Important Health & Safety Information

This class involves the use of lead solder. Because there is no known safe level of lead exposure during pregnancy, this class is not recommended for anyone who is pregnant.

If you are pregnant and interested in learning stained glass, please contact us before registering. In some cases, a lead-free solder option may be available for private events for an additional materials fee.

title: Oak Discovery Day
location: University of California Hopland Research and Extension Center
description:
Visit the Hopland Research and Extension Center for a day of learning and celebration of our local oak woodland ecosystem. Talk to oak experts, sign up for a guided walk, or make an oak inspired craft! This family friendly event will give visitors opportunities to create and explore, while learning more about California's iconic oaks. 

On arrival at the Rod Shippey Hall you will be greeted by an art exhibit of photographs and paintings inspired by our local oaks and shared by the community. A variety of activities and tables will be spread between the woodlands on the patio focused on community science projects, oak woodland management and regeneration, acorn processing, and oak identification. For the kids and everyone looking to unleash their creativity, there will be a large art station featuring sun printing, stamping, painting, and more.

For those wanting to see more of the site, a variety of walks and tours will be held: 

10am-2pm: Oak arts and information booths.

10:30am-12:00pm: Oak Woodland guided walk with naturalist and author Kate Marianchild

10:30am-12:00pm: A Beginners Birding Walk guided by Helen Magruder Menasian

12:30-2:00pm: Nature Journaling with artist and ecologist Robin Lee Carlson

12:30-2:00 pm: Amazing Oaks of Hopland REC with botanist Jen Riddell and UCCE Oak Specialist, Lina Aoyama.

2:30-3:30pm: A performance of And Who Shall Heal the Ground, an original play organized by Quercus Collaborative member Diana Pepetone.

Sliding scale admission from $0-$10 per person.

Snacks will be available, but please bring your own packed lunch to enjoy at the picnic area.

This event is made possible thanks to the support of the Quercus Symbiosis Foundation, and the volunteer group The Quercus Collaborative.

title: Pulp Painting
location: North Bay Letterpress Arts, 925d Gravenstein Hwy South, Sebastopol, CA, 95472, United States
description:
Using finely-beaten, pigmented paper pulp, students will make imagery on freshly pulled sheets of handmade paper. Participants will learn introductory handmade paper techniques such as Western sheet formation, as well as surface design methods of pulp painting, stenciling, and inclusions. When dried, pulp paintings are a part of the paper itself! Elements such as photos, hair, leaves, and newspaper clippings can be embedded into newly made sheets of paper or by using methyl cellulose as an adhesive. 
Please be aware that papermaking is a wet activity – wear clothing and shoes that can get wet. Class involves some physical activity, including standing and arm movements. All supplies are provided through the materials fee. La maestra habla español.

title: Rohnert Park Cotati Reuse + Repair Fair

description:
Do you have a lamp, small appliance, textile, or bike in need of repair?

Bring it to the Reuse \+ Repair Fair!‍ ‍

Volunteers and specialized repair professionals will be on-hand to repair\* your items.  We ask that you stay with your item while it's being fixed, so you can learn tips for future maintenance, how to shop for repairable goods, and even how to repair things yourself!  

If you’d like to bring an item to repair, please register the item here: https://www.reusealliance.org/rf-reg

\(Pre-registering allows us to prepare for your item!\)

This is a free public event.

This event will also include a reuse marketplace, knife sharpening, and a Clothing Swap! Bring clothing and accessories to share and take home something new-to-you. Please limit donations to 1 bag per person \(clean and good condition only, no undergarments or socks please\), but take as much as you’d like! More about clothing swaps here.

\*We cannot guarantee your item\(s\) will be repaired, depending on the existing damage or breakage, ability of volunteer fixers, and availability of materials for repair. Note: we cannot work on microwaves, repair screens on cell phones/computer devices, or perform any welding/brazing, but we are happy to refer you to professionals who can. In addition, the textile department is not able to perform the following:

Replacing zippers

Repairing shoes, leather, or vinyl materials

Performing alterations \(making garments bigger/smaller\)

Replacing rivets/grommets

Hemming certain fabrics \(stretchy fabric, sleek/luxury fabrics e.g. prom dresses\)

If you are in need of garment hemming, we require that you please pin your garment to the desired length before you arrive.

Join Us!

Do you enjoy fixing things?  Or want to help out in other ways?  We need you! Sign up here: https://www.reusealliance.org/rf-volunteer

or email volunteer@reusealliance.org if you have any questions.

At 11 AM and 3 PM each day, Barny will lead a special Studio Tour & Demonstration, sharing the tools and techniques behind his direct-carving process. Visitors can see how he carves and polishes stone, learn about the tools of the trade, and even pick up a hammer and chisel and try carving marble themselves.

With more than 45 years as a sculptor, Barny has created over 1,000 sculptures, working with more than 200 types of stone from around the world.

Come meet the artist, explore the studio and See Art in Action.

title: The Power of Loving Awareness: Meeting Adversity with Compassion & Clarity
location: Spirit Rock Meditation Center
description:
Mindfulness and love are essential and beautiful qualities of an awakened life. Mindfulness leads to clarity, insight, and understanding while compassion is an attitude of heart that cares deeply about life’s challenges. Combined, they allow a kind embrace of the pain and struggles that arise in ourselves, each other, and the world.

During this heartfelt day of meditation, we will discover how these qualities are essential in responding to the inevitable stresses and suffering that are part of being human. We will explore how they are necessary in any journey of awakening and in learning to live wisely and kindly in the midst of difficulty.

Participants will cultivate awareness through mindfulness meditations, and develop a compassionate orientation through heart-opening practices. Teachings will focus on the integration of love and awareness as a response to suffering and pain. We will also inquire into what obstructs the natural expression of the heart.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room

description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Time: 12:00-3:30PM

The invention of the brush in 300 B.C. revolutionized civilization at the time. Up until then, people were carving in stone or bone or writing with sticks in the earth. Because these methods were so slow and unwieldy necessity, the mother of invention, the brush was created.

Please join Christine for this afternoon of brushwork. You will experience three different types of script – formal, semi-cursive and cursive and learn to write five different characters in those styles. At the end of the class you can take your favorite character and write it on a shikishi board.

Christine has studied with several different calligraphy masters over 20 years. She has participated in exhibitions around the world; most recently in San Francisco and Healdsburg. She is the Associate Editor of Heart of the Brush, a collaborative work with Kazuaki Tanahashi, published in 2016. For more information about Christine go to zenbrush.net http://www.zenbrush.net/

title: Using AI to Bring Your Presentation to Life
description:
The Sonoma County Genealogical Society Presents

 Using AI to Bring Your Presentation to Life

 Presented by Jane Pritchard

 Jane will present the slide show she created for the Santa Rosa Chapter of the DAR honoring her Revolutionary War patriot, Margaret Eskridge Kenner, who supported Revolutionary troops with food and supplies. Along the way she taught herself to use AI assistants Claude and Nano Banana, to speed up research and to build both the PowerPoint and a companion PDF. She will walk through the simple, practical ways she used AI — and where it fell short so members can try the same approach with their own ancestors.

Jane began serious family research in 2021, during the pandemic, and has since taken many genealogy classes through Santa Rosa Junior College. She was surprised to discover that her ancestors played a part in the founding of this country — a history her family had never known. That research led to her recent membership in the DAR, where she now serves on the chapter's Lineage Research Committee helping prospective members document their lines. A native of West Virginia, Jane has lived in Santa Rosa since 1981. She is a mother and grandmother and has practiced as a Jin Shin Jyutsu acupressure therapist for 36 years.

A highlight of every tour is the OAEC Nursery, a nonprofit nursery dedicated to uplifting ecologically and culturally important plants. The nursery features a wide selection of perennial food crops, medicinal and native plants, and an ever-evolving collection of annual vegetables and herbs adapted to our region.

location: Copperfield's Books- Petaluma
description:
Join us to celebrate Karen Gebbia's new picture book about waiting patiently! And we'll be serving sweet tea as only our manager can make it, so you won't have to wait for that!

So, what's it about?

Charlotte wants to wait patiently. She really does. But waiting is hard, especially on a stifling Maryland morning, when her t-shirt feels like a hot, heavy blanket, and she can't think of anything but Nana's cold, sweet, lemony, real iced tea.

There are so many steps to Nana's secret recipe tea! Steeping, sugaring, cooling . . . baking muffins to go with it! Nana tells her to find something useful to do while she waits, so Charlotte sweeps, and swings, and snaps pillowcases, but it still isn't ready!

Charlotte has to find more things to do to pass the time, and soon she finds that a day spent waiting can be a day spent enjoying the slower moments. Sometimes the sweetest things in life are the things we have to wait for, and learning to savor them slowly is a joy all its own. Included is a reader's note for adults on helping kids learn how to wait and a secret recipe to try at home.

Author info!

Karen Gebbia is a children's book writer and naturalist based in California. Before writing for children, Karen spent two decades writing, publishing, editing, and teaching scholarly writing.

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
location: Buena Vista Historical Winery
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

description:
Vallejo local singer, Joyce Grant returns to the Ferry Taproom with her powerful mix of jazz, blues, and R&B.

‍Joyce Grant singer/songwriter, is no stranger to Vallejo.  She performs regularly at the Vallejo Ferry Bldg. Taproom, the Coalshed as well as the Benicia Taphouse. A mezzo-soprano with a voice like dark honey, Grant has been singing jazz and R&B in the Bay Area for over 30 years at venues such the Donatello Hotel in San Francisco, the Ledson Hotel in Sonoma, the Empress Theater in Vallejo, Sam’s Chowder House in Half Moon Bay, Nick’s in Pacifica to name a few. She is the great-great-niece of famed ragtime composer Scott Joplin and is a frequent participant in the West Coast Ragtime festival.

For the past 3 years she has been the lead vocalist for the Walnut Creek Jazz Band, an 18- piece big band. As a songwriter she has released the CD In The Morning \(co-produced with Doug McKeehan , 2010\), a collection of original songs ranging in style from jazz to blues to R&B. She continues to bring her sensitive and powerful vocal interpretations to appreciative audiences that keep coming back for more.

title: Claire Wells - Violin with pianist Elizabeth Dorman
description: American violinist Claire Wells, born in 2001, is acclaimed by audiences and the press for her expressive musicality and rich, singing quality of sound. Solo concert engagements have brought her to halls like the Wigmore Hall, the Meyerson Symphony Center, Bass Performance Hall, Teatro Degollado, and Konzerthaus Berlin. Wells plays on a Giovanni Battista Guadagnini, on loan from a generous donor. Having won major prizes in international competitions, Claire Wells is the Mendelssohn-Prize 1st Prize winner and Commission Prize winner at the Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy Competition 2021, 2nd Prize winner at the Michael Hill International Violin Competition 2023, and has taken major prizes at the Indianapolis International Competition, Mirecourt International Competition, Lynn Harrell Competition, among others. Claire Wells grew up in a musical family, playing both violin and piano from the age of three. She studied privately with Brian Lewis, Sandy Yamamoto, and Emanuel Borok, and in 2017 attended the Yehudi Menuhin School with Lutsia Ibragimova. In 2020, Claire Wells studied with Mihaela Martin at the Hochschule für Musik und Tanz Köln. Wells has performed with major orchestras such as the Dallas Symphony Orchestra, Konzerthausorchester Berlin, the Fort Worth Symphony Orchestra, the Belgrade Philharmonic Orchestra, the Jalisco Philharmonic, the Shen Zhen Symphony Orchestra, among others. A passionate chamber musician, Claire Wells has worked alongside majoartists such as Enrico Pace, Nobuko Imai, Frans Helmerson, Christian Tetzlaff, and Steven Isserlis. Wells has also taken coachings from the likes of Ana Chumachenco, Boris Kuschnir, Andras Schiff and Robert Levin. Claire Wells has performed at festivals such as the International Holland Music Sessions, Music@Menlo chamber music festival, Chamber Music Connects the World, Gstaad Festival, the Verbier Festival, and others.

title: Healdbsburg
location: Little Saint
description:
The last few years have been transformative for Nate Amos. Between delivering breakout records both as a solo artist — under his This Is Lorelei moniker — and with his band Water From Your Eyes, sold out shows across multiple continents, to seeing some of today’s most influential artists cover his songs, the ascending songwriter has found his stride.

2024’s Box for Buddy, Box for Star was Amos’ first attempt at an intentionally written full-length solo album, tackling newfound sobriety through a roving tongue-in-cheek take on musical personas, all strained through Amos’ genre-agnostic lens. It was a critical and word-of-mouth success, spawning a deluxe version with covers and collaborations including MJ Lenderman, Hayley Williams, Jeff Tweedy, Cameron Winter and many more.

For many years, Amos’ This Is Lorelei project was known only to a close knit group of creatives in Chicago, where he relocated in his early 20s and produced hundreds of albums and EP’s, tracing the outlines for both of his prolific projects before relocating to New York. In the time since, he’s flourished as a wildly creative polymath who is equally adept at slinging heart worn hooks and eyeball-exploding art-pop.

title: Tribute to Dr. Ralph Stanley with Nathan Stanley Band and Mission Blue
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental, CA 95465
description:
Nathan Stanley Band and Mission Blue honor the King of Mountain Soul
Join us for a musical tribute to the one and only Dr. Ralph Stanley!
Local bluegrass favorites
Mission Blue
open for the touring
Nathan Stanley Band
.
Yes- Nathan is Ralph Stanley's grandson!
Don't miss this incredible evening of unforgettable harmonies and picking from the legendary musical catalog of Ralph Stanley.
Tickets are $30 GA, $25 for OCA members. Online sales end at 6PM day of show or when sold out. This event will be held indoors. ADA seating available, please email info@occidentalcenterforthearts.org to arrange. Beer, wine, refreshments available. Art gallery open during intermission.
Get Tickets
Legendary American bluegrass artist,
Dr. Ralph Edmund Stanley
, was internationally known for his unique, innovative style of singing and banjo playing. In 1976, he was awarded an honorary Doctorate of Music from Lincoln Memorial University, spawning the popular title “Dr. Ralph Stanley.” He was inducted into the International Music Hall of Honor in 1992, and the Grand Ole Opry in 2000, the same year in which his work was featured in the film
O Brother, Where Art Thou?
- for which he won a 2002 Grammy Award for Best Male Country Vocal Performance.
After considering retirement and even scheduling a farewell tour in 2014, Ralph Stanley later announced a welcome decision to continue gracing the country with his beloved, signature style of music.
On June 23, 2016, Dr. Ralph Stanley passed away while battling complications from skin cancer. He will forever be remembered in the hearts and minds of his family and fans, and his legend lives on through his music, which will inspire generations of artists to come.
Read more about Dr. Ralph Stanley here
.
Nathan Stanley is the grandson of Bluegrass Music Icon Dr. Ralph Stanley
and is no exception to the family tradition. Having garnered several charting singles in Inspirational Country Music and Southern Gospel Music, Nathan has come front and center as a music Evangelist.
Through decades of performing—spanning the U.S. and international tours—Nathan has achieved numerous milestones. In 2006, he performed for the Queen of England, and in 2011, his single “White Dove” (featuring Vince Gill) reached #1 on the Inspirational country music charts. That same year, his album “My Kind of Country” was named Classic Country Album of the Year by the National Traditional Country Music Association.
Read more about Nathan Stanley.
Mission Blue has quickly become one of Sonoma County's most beloved bluegrass bands,
delivering their special brand of rhythm, instrumental craft, and harmony singing. A deep well of tradition informs Mission Blue’s sets – one can expect songs from the The Stanley Brothers, Larry Sparks, Bill Monroe, Flatt & Scruggs, Mac Martin and Red Allen, as well as bluegrass innovators such as J.D. Crowe and The New South, Hot Rize, Southern Blend and The Johnson Mountain Boys. They also salt each set with reinterpretations of country hits, folk songs and ballads. Based in Sonoma County, their traditional 5-piece format features Dana Frankel on fiddle, AJ Frankel on guitar, Sam Reed on banjo, David Thiessen on mandolin, and Tom Sours on bass fiddle.
Read more about Mission Blue.

title: S.R. Laws
location: Bloom Carneros
description:
S.R. Laws: An inspiring Storyteller in Song

        S.R. Laws is a performing and recording original musical artist whose work resonates with a familiar warmth while introducing entirely fresh ideas. Hailed by guitarist/promoter Scotty O’Neill as “an ORIGINAL songwriter who knows how to tell a story clearly in song,” Laws has built a reputation for songs that capture both nostalgia and innovation.

Early Influences and Musical Roots  

Growing up in Northern California, Laws developed a deep bond with music at an early age. His father worked as a trash collector, and young Scott Ray Laws \(a.k.a. S.R. Laws\) spent countless hours digging through discarded 45-rpm records. Each discovery—whether caked in grime or found pristine—felt like unearthing treasure. The thrill of dropping the needle on something new ignited his lifelong passion for song-craft.

The Texas Pilgrimage  

With only two suitcases and $500 to his name, Laws set out for Austin, Texas—the “Live Music Capital of the World.” There, open‐mic nights and songwriter showcases became his classroom. Night after night, he honed his craft, forging connections and absorbing the essence of Americana, roots rock, and modern folk.

 “It was such a treat catching your set last night—really refreshing to hear something new and original. Thanks for pulling up a chair and hanging out with us—we really enjoyed the conversation and the stories behind your songs.” - Tripp B., Singer-Songwriter

Influences That Shaped His Voice  

Laws draws inspiration from master storytellers who paved the way for heartfelt, lyrical music. Artists who have left an indelible mark on his craft include:

- John Hiatt  

- Lucinda Williams  

- Rodney Crowell  

- Neil Finn  

- Patty Griffin  

- Steve Earle  

- Ron Sexsmith  

Their mastery of narrative and melody has shaped his own artistic journey, resulting in songs that feel both comfortingly familiar and entirely “out there.”

Critical Acclaim  

Colleagues and venue owners alike have praised his work and stage presence:  

“Scott Ray Laws is a unique and really cool songwriter…he digs into materials, tells a story in his songs, and has a clean baritone vocality that is easy on the ears. We had a chance to meet and hang with Scott back in May…and I had to have him back for a Wednesday evening.” - Luigi, Owner of The Listening Room

“Expect slow-burning passion and vivid music…the kind of energy that turns into ‘let’s stay for just one more!” - Doug, Owner/Wine Maker at Spicy Vines

Current Projects  

Now based in Sonoma County, California, Laws works tirelessly as a recording, writing & touring artist. Through over 100 gig dates a year, intimate club shows, festival stages, house concerts and late-night songwriter circles, he invites audiences to join him on a musical journey—one heartfelt story at a time.

With a blend of classic influence, modern vision, and a voice that feels like home, S.R. Laws continues to carve out his place in the American songwriting landscape.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Meeting
description:
Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.

In OA, members experience spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery by practicing the Twelve Steps and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

Overeaters Anonymous \(OA\) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person meetings at 9:30 on Sunday mornings at Church of the Nazarene, 18980 Arnold Drive, Sonoma, CA \(a small room directly off of parking lot; look for the sign posted\) and newcomers are always welcome.

You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

OA is not a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does not endorse any specific food plan. 

Visit: https://www.northbayoa.org/

Find a meeting: https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: "Paddle The Petaluma: Turn to The River" Guided Kayak Tour
location: The Floathouse Petaluma
description:
Paddle the Petaluma: Turn to The River is a relaxed, beginner-friendly guided kayak tour exploring the past, present, and future of Petaluma’s historic waterway. Launching right from downtown at The Floathouse Petaluma, you'll take part in this Sonoma County Signature Experience by spending about 90 minutes on the water in stable sit-on-top kayaks, traveling a gentle mile-and-a-half route through “Petaluma’s Longest Park.”

Along the way, you’ll raft up at docks around town, fascinating  landmarks, and riverfront gathering spaces to hear stories about how this Gold Rush-era “saltwater highway” helped shape Petaluma—and how today’s community is continuing to reinvent and reconnect with the river. This isn’t just a history tour. You’ll also learn about the people, businesses, artists, nonprofits, and river advocates helping shape the waterway’s future right now.

Everything is included in the $75 experience: kayak, gear, knowledgeable local guides, insider river stories, and post-paddle perks at nearby businesses. Finish with plenty of time for brunch, coffee, shopping, or simply hanging out downtown by the water. No experience necessary.

Note: The Floathouse Petaluma is a nonprofit project dedicated to “putting butts in boats and smiles on faces” by offering year-round easy access to the Petaluma River in and on people-powered water craft through rentals, events, classes, lessons and summer camps.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: The Embodied Mind: The Somatic Language of Thoughts and Emotions
location: Spirit Rock Meditation Center
description:
with Jill Satterfield

Emerging research on the predictive aspect of the nervous system suggests the body doesn’t just react to our thoughts and emotions — it can and does anticipate them, generating predictions that may shape what we’re about to feel and think even before we’ve consciously registered it. The hair rising on the back of your neck, a gut feeling before you know why: these are signs of the nervous system registering and responding to signals caring for us, before they’ve been consciously processed as thought or story. What we experience as spontaneous is often the tail end of a process that began in the body moments earlier. This daylong workshop trains attention on that predictive layer and develops interoception, or internal awareness, the felt sense arising in real time prior to story or interpretation. We’ll explore meditation and mindfulness practices along with self – guided breathing as a bridge between body and mind — to build sensitivity to early signals of the raw data that the nervous system is constantly generating. Through breathwork and nervous-system-informed relaxation techniques, we’ll practice intervening at the point of origin, where there is still room to choose a different response rather than being carried by a habit reaction, already set in motion.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
location: Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

title: Book Launch With Sonoma County Author Karen Gebbia
location: Russian River Books & Letters
description:
You can't rush real iced tea. Charlotte wants to wait patiently. She really does. But waiting is hard, especially on a stifling Maryland morning, when her t-shirt feels like a hot, heavy blanket, and she can't think of anything but Nana's cold, sweet, lemony, real iced tea.

There are so many steps to Nana's secret recipe tea! Steeping, sugaring, cooling . . . baking muffins to go with it! Nana tells her to find something useful to do while she waits, so Charlotte sweeps, and swings, and snaps pillowcases, but it still isn't ready!

Charlotte has to find more things to do to pass the time, and soon she finds that a day spent waiting can be a day spent enjoying the slower moments. Sometimes the sweetest things in life are the things we have to wait for, and learning to savor them slowly is a joy all its own. Included is a reader's note for adults on helping kids learn how to wait and a secret recipe to try at home.

Scavenger Hunt and Stickers for the kiddos.

title: I Need a Mic: Open Mic
location: City Arts Gallery
description:
Welcome poets, writers, and artists of Vallejo. My name is Ray, and I am your host of I NEED A MIC OPEN MIC.

This is more than just a stage — it’s a space. A space where voices rise, stories breathe, and truth finds its rhythm. 

Whether you carry poems in your chest, songs in your spirit, or stories that have been waiting for the right moment — this is your invitation.

We gather not just to perform, but to connect. To celebrate the raw, the real, and the unapologetically human art of expression. Every voice matters here. Every perspective adds to the pulse of this room.

But understand — this is a space built on respect. While we welcome passion, depth, and honesty, we do not tolerate hate, disrespect, or harmful rhetoric. Heavy political agendas that divide rather than inspire have no place here. 

This stage is for expression, not oppression.

Bring your truth. Bring your courage. Bring your art.

Come share. Come listen. Come feel something.

Because someone in that room might need exactly what you have to say.

I NEED A MIC — and maybe, so do you.

title: No Cell Sundays: Callie Watts & Kris Dilbeck
location: Hook & Ladder Winery
description:
**Callie Watts: Where Classic Sounds Meet Modern Soul**

Join us for No Cell Sundays with Callie Watts, a Northern California pop singer-songwriter whose sound is steeped in the golden era of songwriting.

Raised on classical music, The Beatles, and The Beach Boys, Callie discovered her calling through the great writers of the '60s and '70s—Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, and Carole King. These legendary artists shaped her melodic writing style and continue to influence every note she plays.

A versatile musician, Callie has spent her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, arranger, and lead/backing vocalist—performing solo and with local and Bay Area bands across multiple genres. Expect an afternoon of soulful melodies, timeless classics, and songs that transport you back to when music was everything.

**What's No Cell Sundays?**

It's simple: disconnect from your devices, reconnect with great wine, live music, and the people around you. *Check your phone with us at the door and receive a complimentary tasting.* Bring a blanket, grab a glass, and spend your Sunday the way it was meant to be spent.

title: Reuse in Art, Reuse in Life: A Conversation Between Ali Gass and Phoebe Schenker
location: Petaluma Arts Center
description:
Join Alison Gass, Founding Executive Director of the ICA San Francisco, and Phoebe Schenker, Executive Director of Reuse Alliance, for a wide-ranging conversation about reuse in contemporary and historical art and why it is more relevant than ever.

The discussion will explore the many ways artists have engaged with reuse, from incorporating found and reclaimed materials to making reuse itself a central subject of their work. Together, Gass and Schenker will consider how reuse connects to broader cultural conversations about creativity, sustainability, consumption, and value, while also exploring how reuse can become a creative practice in our own everyday lives.

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
location: Buena Vista Historical Winery
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: Marking the Flesh: Revealing the Tattoo Practices of the Nile Valley
location: Student Center - Petaluma Campus
description: The North Coast Chapter of the Archaeological Institute of America invites you to the following lecture:  Marking the Flesh: Revealing the Tattoo Practices of the Nile ValleyAbstract: For more than a century, archaeologists knew that some ancient Egyptians and Nubians had tattoos—but only a few tattooed people had been identified across Egypt and Nubia's vast ancient history.  Over the past decade, however, new technology and growing interest have dramatically changed our evidence for and understanding of tattooing. This lecture will share the stories of these tattooed people and the remarkable legacy of tattoo practices they represent—a tradition that began over 5,000 years ago and continues today.*Dr. Anne Austin is an Associate Professor of History at the University of Missouri St. Louis (UMSL). Her research combines the fields of osteology and Egyptology in order to document medicine and disease in the past.  Event Details:  • Sunday, October 18, 2026, SRJC Petaluma Student Center (https://maps.santarosa.edu/student-center), 4:00-5:15 p.m.  • This lecture is free and open to the public  • *This presentation may contain images of human remains.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting in Santa Rosa
location: Christ Church United Methodist
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: Slow Meditative Birding Journey
location: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
description:
Do you enjoy a slow walk in a valley, breezes, wildflowers, the sounds of songbirds, the taste of a Douglas Fir needle or a California Bay leaf, the aroma of Tarweed, or watching wild turkeys and California Quail hunt for seeds and insects in the grass? Join Certified California Naturalists and Sugarloaf docents for this series of meandering explorations. Each month (weather permitting) we will explore one or two of our three accessible trails-- the Creekside Trail, the Nature Trail, and the Meadow trail. Suitable for all levels and a range of mobility, these Sunday afternoon adventures will accommodate people using walkers or wheelchairs, young children, parents with babies in strollers, as well as those who just enjoy slow walks in nature that stimulate the five senses. 

Our October outing will focus on meditative birding. We will start off by sitting quietly for 10 minutes with Merlin app recording in 3 different locations, followed by about 10 minutes of discussion of the birds we heard, using Cornell to confirm their calls and songs before moving onto the next sitting spot. We will also saunter (while looking for birds) between the locations for a total distance of ~1.3 miles on an accessible trail. Birding by ear lends itself to meditation because it works best when you sit silently and listening closely (i.e., if Merlin *hears* something you did not, it reminds you that your mind has wandered). 

Tickets are $5 for adults and free for children under 18 years of age. All minors must be accompanied by parent or legal guardian. **Tickets day-of, on site will be $10 and might not be available.** Meet at the White Barn parking lot.

title: Rata Blanca en
location: LA HACIENDA DEL TORO
description:
Rata Blanca

 

 Wálter Giardino: guitarra

 Adrián Barilari: voz

 Fernando Scarcella: batería

 Guillermo Sánchez: bajo

 Hugo Bistolfi: teclados

 

 Mas de tres millones de discos vendidos en el mundo hacen de esta banda la mas influyente en la historia del rock en castellano.

 Respetados en todo el mundo han sabido llevar su musica a lo mas alto desde que salieron de las calles del Bajo Flores,un peligroso barrio en el sur de Buenos Aires.

 Su historia es grande y sigue creciendo como una leyenda de la mano del guitarrista Walter Giardino,considerado entre los mejores del mundo.

 

  

 

 

 

 Debutaron en el teatro de Luz y Fuerza ante 600 personas, el 15 de agosto de 1987. Walter Giardino armó este grupo metálico tras su  paso por V8 y pasaron casi dos años de ensayos antes de salir a tocar. 

 

 Participaron del festival "Halley en Obras", junto a Alakrán, JAF y Kamikaze, en junio de 1988. Ese año lograron editar el álbum debut, que tuvo dos temas de difusión: "Chico callejero" y "El sueño de la gitana". El primer disco de la banda fue presentado el 18 de diciembre en el teatro Alfil y llego a ser rapidamente disco de oro.

 

 A comienzos del año siguiente Adrián Barilari reemplazó a Saúl Blanch y se incorporó Hugo Bistolfi en los teclados. Con esa formación editaron "Magos, espadas y rosas"\(1990\), que pudieron presentar masivamente en el show de en Obras.

 Magos espadas y rosas llego a ser disco triple platino,algo unico y jamas repetido ni de cerca por alguna otra banda de hard rock o metal latinoamericana. 

 

 Con su estilo unico alcanzaron en 1991 su pico de mayor popularidad, al vender más de 200 mil copias de su tres discos, apoyados en sus 120 shows por todo el país. El año se coronó con un concierto en Velez ante 30.000 personas.

 

 Una gran parte del repertorio posee una fuerte identificación con la música clásica, sin perder la fuerza metálica que los caracteriza. Es por ello que en el cierre de la "Gira Guerrera" \(octubre del '92 en el Opera\), se presentaron con una orquesta de cuerdas e interpretaron un preludio de Johann Sebastian Bach y un fragmento de la Primavera de Vivaldi. La puesta tuvo el agregado de un video wall de nueve pantallas. 6.700 personas atendieron las tres funciones.

 

 «Rata Blanca hizo de todo - explica Giardino -Rata Blanca pasó por arriba todos los prejuicios, a las grabadoras, un montón de gente vivió de Rata Blanca y ganó dinero y haciendo que el heavy metal, inconscientemente, subiera a puestos inesperados e inalcanzables hasta ese momento. Y hoy todavía ninguna banda de heavy metal pudo hacer ni la mitad de lo que hicimos nosotros. Si hay tipos tan capaces, no se dónde están, porque no salen a tocar ni a la esquina» \(F.Blumetti / C.Parise, pág 146\). Rata Blanca sí salía a tocar: cuatro fechas promedio por fin de semana, teatros y locales de bailantas que alquilaban especialmente para poder tocar ante un publico que no podia verlos en capital federal \(hecho éste por el cual fueron muy criticados en un comienzo, pese a meter 4000 personas por show\). «Nos dijeron caretas cuando nos fue bien y grasas cuando tocamos en bailantas. Pero soy del pueblo y fui a tocar para el pueblo» \(Giardino al Sí de Clarín, 1/12/95\).

 

 "Entre el cielo y el infierno" \(1994\) fue grabado en España con Mario Ian \(ex Alakrán\) y presentado en una gira latinoamericana. Fueron invitados a tocar en el festival Mosters of Rock de San Pablo, junto a Ozzy Osbourne, Therapy? Y Alice Cooper, en septiembre de 1995.

 

 En 1997 concretaron otro cambio de cantante: Gabriel Marian \(ex-Escocia\) reemplazó a Ian, luego de un casting de más de 100 vocalistas. Con esta formación editaron el séptimo disco, titulado simplemente "Rata Blanca", con la intención de recuperar el terreno perdido en los tres años de ausencia en las bateas.

 

 Giardino confirmó la separación de la banda en abril del '98. «La falta de promoción del último disco aceleró la decisión, pero es cierto que no estábamos pasando por el mejor momento». Editó su primer disco solista en 1999.

 

 En octubre del 2000 se reunieron para realizar una gira por Latinoamérica \(Bolivia, Chile, México, Colombia y Ecuador\). Se presentaron también en Buenos Aires y editaron un disco recopilación, que incluye una versión acústica de "Mujer amante" como bonus track.

 

 "El camino del fuego" fue el disco del nuevo reencuentro, editado en el 2002, con Giardino en guitarra, Barilari en voz, Bistolfi en teclados, Guillermo Sánchez en bajo y Fernando Scarcella en batería. Además, ese mismo año editaron dos simples.

 Este disco fue platino,algo que no sucedia en el estilo desde la separacion de Rata Blanca.

 

 "La llave de la puerta secreta" fue el disco número 12 en la carrera de la banda. «Es un disco típico de Rata Blanca. Muy metalero, con alguna balada como siempre. Y también hay un blues, algo inédito en nosotros», explicaba Adrián Barilari. «Hemos puesto toda la tecnología de hoy en día en beneficio de ese sonido de los '90. Casi vintage. El disco suena como "Magos, espadas y rosas" o "Guerreros del arco iris"». La temática de las letras está basada, en gran parte, en el libro "El código Da Vinci".

 Hoy este disco tambien es platino.

 

 Actualmente el grupo se encuentra trabajando el el proximo album que se podra conseguir a mediados del mes de Mayo,segun se dice.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

location: Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center
description:

[[breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com](mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com)]([mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com](http://mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com/)), 707-235-1413

**Talasana Krama (Foundational Sequence) & Pranayama**

**$25, Discounted Class Passes & Sliding Scale Available**
Fundamental practices for understanding the holistic nature, energetics and Sanskrit yoga philosophy guiding the approach of this comprehensive system. Long time yoga practitioners as well as new students will benefit. Experience the distinction of this system verses other modern yoga/vinyasa practices commonly taught & the traditional & precise use of ujjayi breath as it relates to the Sanskrit parameters, moving with the breath and the importance of the pause. Talasana is a very unique & profound krama initiating & establishing "samasthiti", the steadiness and focus of mind, balanced energy and steadiness of body - with the two feet together, moving from the center, all the major joints and muscles of the body are exercised using arm and hand movements, back bends, side bends, twists, forward bends, squats and balancing foot stretches. The fingers interlaced create a prana circuit as they come together in the repetitive movement over the head. The breath specific movements stretch the diaphragm, psoas, massage the heart and internal organs, clear the lungs, drain the lymphatic system, stimulate the vagus nerve and calm the mind. Energy is created along the spine and central nervous system, and is distributed throughout the nadis and into the entire energy body. Regular practice of Talasana flowers into to ananta samapatti and understanding "stillness in movement".
Class begins with Opening Mantras & Ding Namaskar (Devotional Salutation to the Directional Spheres with Breath & Mantra). Then moves to Tāĺāsana to Savasana then Seated Prānāyāma (Yogic Breathing) including Morning Cleansing Kriyas, Ujjayi, Nadi Shuddi, Samantraka Prānāyāma, Pratyahara, Dharana. May include Specific Mudra (Energetic Bodily Gestures).

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Jumpstart Your Art
description: Every person experiences an ebb and flow to the tides of their creativity. We will share space together to design, exchange ideas, and hold ourselves accountable to our unique interests! The first portion of our time together will involve a check-in discussion of ‘what is', leading into ‘what could be'. The talk will be facilitated by Erin Partridge, an art therapist with a long history of supporting people in reengaging with creativity. After our initial talk, we will have some time to individually focus on our creative practices in the space of the gallery. Before we close, we will share anything that came up in the process. title: Meet + Greet: Bunns Rabbit II by Alan Barillaro
description: Join us for a special meet-and-greet event with Alan Barillaro, author of Bunns Rabbit II . This event is free, but we appreciate your RSVP below so we can plan for your attendance. ABOUT THE BOOK One adventure has ended, only for a new epic journey to begin . . . Author-illustrator and Academy Award–winning filmmaker Alan Barillaro takes his storytelling and artwork to new heights in a compelling sequel. When Bunns Rabbit returns from her quest to find the Spirit Fox, she hopes to go back to her quiet life among her family. But Fox has other plans for her. A war is on the horizon, pitting the Spirits of the Sea and Wind against those of the Land and Fire. According to Fox, only one little rabbit stands in their way—her. This time there is more than just her family on the line. It is up to Bunns to save every living creature on the land before they are washed away by the sea forever. With war imminent and newly acquired powers she barely understands, Bunns must avert disaster and find it within herself to stand up and face this new world, whether she is ready to or not. With his inviting prose, warm illustrations, and dramatic graphic panels, Alan Barillaro brings another action- packed tale of daring, bravery, and adventure, filled with heart, kindness, and hope. ABOUT THE AUTHOR Alan Barillaro is an acclaimed author, illustrator, and Academy Award-winning filmmaker whose work spans the worlds of picture books, middle grade novels and animation. Born in Canada and now living in California, he spent over two decades at Pixar Animation Studios, working as a supervising animator on many popular theatrical releases, including The Incredibles, Incredibles 2, WALL·E, and Brave. In 2016 he directed Piper — a short film about a tiny sandpiper learning to face her fears — which won the Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film. Now he brings those same storytelling instincts to his novels and illustrated books, telling tender, humorous, deeply felt stories for the small readers in all of us.

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting

description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Mondays
location: Salsa Dance Marin
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.
